features: Town held by Marsilion, eventually taken by the French.
Pass where Roland and his forces were ambushed by the Saracens.
Spanish town known for blacksmiths’ work; the shield of the Saracen knight Malquiant was made there.
A Saracen lord, killed by Archbishop Turpin.
Town in southern France sacked by Roland.
A Saracen baron; count of Tortelosa; killed by Oliver in the first battle.
One of Twelve Peers, the Gascon of Bordeaux; the most valiant knight, killed by Climborin in the first battle.
One of the Twelve Peers; kills Malprimis; killed by Grandoyne.
Brother of King Marsilion; killed by Oliver.
A Saracen lord from Brigale; killed by Gerin in the first battle.
Spanish town ruled by Count Turgis.
French count; stepfather of Roland; brother-in-law of Roland’s uncle Charlemagne; betrays Roland and the French rear guard to Marsilion.
Queen of Saragossa, wife of Marsilion.
Tibbald of Reims; French baron; guarded French dead at Roncevaux.
Charlemagne's nephew; led rear guard of French forces; hero in song of Roland.
Saracen king of Spain; Roland wounds him and he died of wound later.
A French baron; ruled over Valence on Rhone.
A Saracen lord; killed by Oliver.
Guarded French dead while Charlemagne pursued Saracen forces.
Roland's friend; mortally wounded by Marganice.
French knight; Duke of Argonne; brother of Godefroy, Charlemagne’s standard bearer. At Ganelon's trial, Thierry alone insists on Ganelon's guilt.
Son of Marsilion, Saracen king of Spain.
Frankish baron, one of the Twelve Peers.
Dane who led 3rd column in Charlemagne's army against Baligant's forces.
Joint Commander of Charlemagne's Eighth Division.
Emperor of France and Germanic nations; his forces fought the Saracens in Spain.
A French baron; takes Roland’s place at vanguard of Charlemagne’s forces; leads first column.
Archbishop of Rheims in Song of Roland.
One of twelve peers; guarded French dead while Charlemagne pursued Saracen forces; sixth column leader.
Town in Spain taken by Charlemagne.
One of twelve peers; killed Estramarin; killed by Grandoyne.
Saracen lord and emissary to Charles.
Pinabel of Sorence, a French baron, Ganelon's kinsmen and skilled speaker. Large and powerful, he agrees to fight Thierry to settle the issue of Ganelon's guilt and he lost the judicial combat.
Guarded French dead; became leader of Charlemagne's 2nd column.
Charlemagne’s officer who hung Ganelon’s 30 relatives.
French baron; Murdered while serving as Ambassador of Marsilon.
Saracen lord from Seville; volunteered to fight at Roncevaux Pass.
Saracen lord; volunteered to fight at Roncevaux Pass; killed Archbishop Turpin in the first battle.
Emir of Babylon; Marsilion enlisted his help against Charlemagne.
Spanish town whose walls Roland had shattered.
Son of Cappadocian King Capuel; killed Gerin, Gerier, Berenger, Guy St. Antoine, Duke Astorge; killed by Roland.
Johun of Outremer; Saracen lord and emissary to Charles.
Standard bearer of Charlemagne; brother of Tierri, Charlemagne's defender against Pinabel.
Saracen lord and emissary to Charles.
A Saracen lord; killed by Gerin and Gerier in the first battle.
Marsilion’s nephew, killed by Roland in the first battle.
Chief cook for Charlemagne's army; he guarded Ganelon after Ganelon's treachery was discovered.
Escremiz comes from this Spanish town.
Saracen lord who gave his helmet to Ganelon; killed by Oliver.
A Saracen king from Lycia; leader in Baligant’s army.
Shares command of Charlemagne’s sixth division; leader of part of the 5th column.
Saracen lord, gave his sword to Ganelon.
One of the Twelve Peers; kills Turgis; killed by Malquiant.
A French baron; killed by Marsilion.
Saracen lord and emissary to Charles.
Place in Spain near which Basan and Basilie were murdered by Marsilion.
French commander of one of first divisions against Baligant; killed by Baligant.
One of 12 peers, killed by Marsilion.
Saracen lord and emissary to Charles.
Aceline of Gascony, one of the Twelve Peers, the council of King Charles.
French baron, Duke of Burgundy; one of the Twelve Peers; killed by Valdebron.
Saracen lord, one of the Saracen Twelve Peers.
Saracen lord and emissary to Charles.
Leader in Baligant’s army; king of Persia; killed by Rabel.
French baron; murdered near Haltile with his brother Basan while serving as ambassador to Marsilion.
Escremiz of Valterne; volunteered to fight at Roncevaux Pass; killed by Engelier in the first battle.
Italian-French astronomer who discovered Iapetus in 1671, Rhea in 1672, Tethys and Dione in 1684 (1625-1712).
